claims.text: The stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is governed by an interplay between thermal-expansion anisotropy and evolving nanoscale compositional heterogeneities.
Changing the cooling rate after cycling to 1250 °C produces different levels of thermal-expansion mismatch.
Changing the cooling rate after cycling to 1250 °C produces different levels of nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneities are associated with lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal-expansion mismatch during thermal cycling induces localized stresses.
The localized stresses caused by thermal-expansion mismatch interact with nanoscale compositional heterogeneities.
The interaction between localized stresses and compositional heterogeneities changes dislocation mobility.
Changes in dislocation mobility alter the alloy's stress–strain behavior.
Nanoscale compositional heterogeneities alter local bonding environments.
Changes in local bonding environments caused by compositional heterogeneity alter the elastic moduli.
Changes in local bonding environments caused by compositional heterogeneity alter the thermal-expansion coefficients.
Faster cooling produces greater thermal-expansion mismatch than furnace cooling.
Faster cooling produces more pronounced nanoscale compositional heterogeneities than furnace cooling.
Faster-cooled samples will have higher yield strength than furnace-cooled samples.
Faster-cooled samples will have lower ductility than furnace-cooled samples.
Faster-cooled samples will have different elastic moduli from furnace-cooled samples.
Thermal-expansion coefficients will exhibit greater anisotropy after faster cooling.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature to 1250 °C provided that cooling does not cause macroscopic phase separation or cracking.
